mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5% for 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in employment (PAYEMS) indicates a misalignment between housing demand and labor market strength, causing market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of HOUST decline and PAYEMS rise does not produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term's coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth above 3.0%), corporate earnings are expected to rise, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which supports corporate profits and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising (monthly change > 0), or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it triggers expectations of monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In high interest rate regimes (FEDFUNDS above 4.5%), the cost of capital rises, suppressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.5%) signals an aggressive monetary policy response to a weak labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates stimulus.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 7.5% does not produce positive returns in more than 60% of instances, or the interaction term's coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over 3-year rolling windows.
